# Best Portable Power Stations for Camping

For most tent and car camping, a **250–500Wh station** is the right size. It covers phones, lights, a camera, a fan, and even a CPAP for several nights, and it weighs only 8–10 lb. Go bigger only if you plan to run a 12V fridge or electric cooler, or you're living out of a van. [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)

## Compact picks (weekend tent or car camping)

| Model | Capacity / AC output | Weight | Approx. price | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** | 288Wh / 300W | ~8.3 lb | ~$249 | Best overall. Lightest of the group, very simple, pairs easily with solar. |
| **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** | 286Wh / 600W | ~9.9 lb | ~$269–299 | Best value. Twice the inverter power, and you can expand it to 572Wh. |
| **Anker SOLIX C300** | 288Wh / 300W (600W surge) | ~9.3 lb | ~$199 | Built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the AC version, not the "C300 DC." |
| **Bluetti EB3A** | 268Wh / 600W | ~10.1 lb | ~$179 | Budget pick that still has long-lasting LiFePO4 cells. |

Source and buy links: [PowerStationGearLab's camping guide](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/) has "Check price on Amazon" links for each model. One note: Jackery has replaced the 300 Plus with the **Explorer 300 v2**, which recharges faster but has a shorter warranty. The Plus is still sold on Amazon.

**CPAP tip:** turn the humidifier off. With it off, a ~288Wh unit runs most CPAPs for 3–5 nights. With it on, the machine can draw about three times as much power.

## Bigger picks (fridge, cooler, van, or overland)

- **Bluetti AC180** has 1,152Wh, an 1,800W inverter, and LiFePO4 cells, and weighs about 35 lb. It costs $499, or **$474.05 with code AFF5OFF** (tested at checkout 2026-10-21).
  - **Buy:** https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180
  - This is an affiliate link from [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180).
  - It has no expansion port, and the $599 option is a bundle with a solar panel.
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** is OutdoorGearLab's best value pick. It has 1,800W of output, weighs 25 lb, and is on sale for under $530. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** has 1,070Wh and costs about $799. It's TechRadar's camping pick. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** has 1,536Wh and is IP65 rated against rain and dust, so it suits rough trips. It's about $1,079 on Amazon. It's WIRED's camping pick. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** has 2,042Wh, weighs 39 lb, and is under $900 on Amazon. It's OutdoorGearLab's choice for multi-day off-grid trips. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)

## My quick recommendation

- **Weekend camping with small devices:** Jackery Explorer 300 Plus, or the EcoFlow River 3 Plus if you want more output.
- **Running an electric cooler or fridge:** Anker C1000 Gen 2 or Bluetti AC180.

Black Friday is coming up, so prices may drop soon. What do you plan to power, and for how many nights? I can narrow it down from there.
